dedupe_keys.name: ngfs climate scenarios data set network for greening the financial system phase v

description: The NGFS Climate Scenarios are a set of long-term climate scenarios produced for central banks and financial supervisors, combining transition pathways from integrated assessment models (GCAM, MESSAGE-GLOBIOM and REMIND-MAgPIE), chronic physical impacts from Earth system and climate impact models, acute impacts from natural catastrophe modelling, and macro-financial effects from the NiGEM model. The current phase, version 5 released in November 2024 with a 5.1 data update in March 2026, groups scenarios into orderly, disorderly, hot house world and too little, too late families, including Net Zero 2050, Below 2°C, Delayed Transition, Fragmented World, Current Policies, NDCs and Low Demand, with variables on energy supply and demand, emissions, carbon prices, capacities, GDP and country-level downscaling. They are produced by the NGFS workstream on scenario design with an academic consortium of PIK, IIASA, the University of Maryland, Climate Analytics and NIESR; the NGFS gathers 127 central banks and supervisors. Data are accessible free through the IIASA NGFS Scenario Explorer with a guest login, in multiple formats, and the Zenodo record documents each release. The licence allows research and commercial use but restricts redistribution of substantial parts of the data. Caveats: the physical risk estimates in Phase V rest on a paper (Kotz et al. 2024) that was critiqued and revised, and the NGFS disclaims liability for use. It supports scenario design for long-term infrastructure capacity planning and climate adaptation across energy and other sectors; a related record is ERA5.
